name: PEM: one pooled posterior of edit effects per arm builds macro-edits sized to the acceptance threshold. The discovered generator is then tested by one-step discovery on the four fresh categories.
core_idea: PEM replaces design o's generator with one hierarchical Gaussian model of edit effects per arm. Design o's generator is a softmax over 43 cells, learned per lineage by the parent's CEM from six noisy values a step. The new model is fitted to every paired measurement of every lineage, with terms that are shared across categories, specific to one category, common to one parent and seed, and for CPU. Each step takes six Thompson draws from the model and uses each to compose a macro-candidate of up to K edits, drawn from edit classes the model does not predict to be destructive. The reason is arithmetic: single non-destructive edits have a true-effect sd of about 0.004, while the acceptance threshold is about 0.015 to 0.018, so they essentially never pass. Additive macros of 8 such edits have an sd of about 0.011 and pass in about 0.1 to 0.18 of steps. Three things that are discovered decide the next candidates: the posterior, accepted edit sets offered to the other lineages, and changes to the model's own structure that are adopted on their prospective predictive score. The recursion is tested on the four fresh categories. The final generator is frozen and runs paired one-step discovery episodes against two controls at matched CPU: the original generator, and the same machinery without the discovered knowledge.
why_it_beats_the_measured_limit:
(1) The limit. Knapsack is replaced by bin packing (knapsack carries no signal). Bin packing's paired sd of 0.0064 is an assumption (sqrt(2) x its run sd 0.0045) and is measured in development. The 16 confirmation pairs then have a pooled sd of sqrt((0.021^2+0.039^2+0.006^2+0.0064^2)/4) = 0.0226 and an SE of the mean of 0.0056. Under the registered rule (t >= 2.6, mean >= 0.0025) that gives 50% power at a 4-category effect of 0.0147 and 80% at 0.019. Candidates whose effect differs between categories, as measured (per-category effects nearly uncorrelated), have that between-category spread enter the t statistic. For 8-edit macros with a shared fraction of 0.1, the sample sd rises to about 0.028, the 50% point to about 0.018 and the 80% point to about 0.023.
(2) What G0 can deliver. Among candidates that screened positive, the screen-promotion correlation is 0.10, with noise sds of 0.011 (one seed) and 0.008 (two seeds). That implies a true-effect sd of about 0.0032 (about 0.004 before range restriction). The rest of the measured sd of 0.032 comes from destructive cells: score/replace -0.28, score/mutop -0.15, pick/swap -0.059, propose/replace -0.040, score/swap -0.037, shortlist -0.027. Best-of-step selection with promotion reliability 0.2 predicts a confirmed value of about +0.001, which matches the measured +0.0012. Using the measured confirmation rate (4 of 29 steps) and P(pass | confirmed) of about Phi((0.0012-0.0147)/0.0069) = 0.025, F should accept about 0.0035 per step: 0.07 per lineage of 20 steps, or 0.3 per arm, mostly of near-zero effects.
(3) What macros can deliver. For k additive non-destructive edits the sd is 0.004*sqrt(k), so 0.0113 at k = 8. Screening keeps the top 3 of 6 (reliability 0.5) and promotion picks the best (reliability within the kept set 0.5). The selected candidate's expected true effect is then about 0.0104, with a posterior sd of about 0.0065. The pass probability is about Phi((0.0104-0.0183)/0.0086) = 0.18 per step. It is about 0.11 if the promotion values carry the shift that the measured confirmation rate implies, and about 0.085 if the single-edit sd is 0.003. It is about 0.23 at k = 12, about 0.45 if the kept edits average +0.001 each, and 0.03 if they average -0.001. Destructive cells are excluded once the posterior gives P(effect < -0.01) > 0.8, which takes 3 to 5 measurements at their sizes. k_max grows with the data. So after about 5 lineage-steps of learning, about 15 productive steps give about 2 acceptances per lineage (range 0.4 to 7), or about 8 per arm, against about 0.3 for F.
(4) False acceptance. The rule is unchanged, and the model sees the confirmation seeds only after the decision is recorded, so the rate stays at about 1% or less per confirmation (registered stub calibration: 0.0083 to 0.0103 per step in the worst case). R confirms in about half its steps, so it expects about 0.1 false acceptances per lineage. This must be recalibrated with stub runs for macros and the new noise profile.
(5) What it cannot fix. On four source categories, acceptance mostly selects category-specific effect. The held-out value of an accepted macro is only its shared part, about 0 to 0.003. The capability endpoint (4 fresh categories x 8 seeds: SE about 0.004 within categories, a category-resampling interval of about +/-0.01, detectable effects of about 0.012 or more) is therefore predicted not to be met.
(6) The recursion endpoint. Y1 is the confirmed 16-pair mean of an episode's selected candidate, measured on part B with 4 fresh seeds (0 if no candidate is ready). Predicted Y1: G* about +0.005, G0 about +0.0002. The per-episode sd of the paired difference is about 0.0095. With 24 episodes the SE is 0.0019, so one-sided power is about 0.84 for a difference of +0.005 and about 0.47 for +0.003. Smallest detectable difference at 80% power: about 0.0047.
(7) CPU: at most 209,000 of the 300,000 CPU-s available.
All numbers are analytic approximations from the brief's measurements, not simulated (see the implementation plan).
recursion:
The discovered results change generation in three ways.
Route 1, learned knowledge changes generation. Every paired measurement of every lineage of the arm is added to one posterior: screening, promotion, and confirmation once its decision is recorded. The next step's six macros come from six Thompson draws of that posterior. Earlier measurements therefore decide:
- which cells, operations, sensors, constants and scalar values appear, and with which sign;
- how many edits a macro holds: the limit k_max(n) = min(K_MAX, 1 + n // 12) grows with the arm's count of measured candidates, and within it the composer takes the size that maximises the posterior probability that the 4-category effect exceeds the target 0.018;
- which cells are never proposed again (posterior P(effect < -0.01) > 0.8).
Route 2, discovered mechanisms change generation. An accepted mechanism becomes its lineage's parent and its live blocks enter the library. Its whole edit set, as a diff, is offered to the arm's other lineages as one transplant unit (recombination). Its acceptance count enters the parent-context features, so later edits are re-predicted relative to it.
Route 3, the generator improves itself. Every 8 pooled steps, three single-edit variants of the model's structure are proposed: feature group on/off, a group's prior scale halved or doubled, the category term on/off, the interaction term on/off, or the data window. Each variant is fitted only on data from before a window and scored on that window's screening values by log predictive density, paired per candidate. A variant is adopted if its paired t >= 2.6 over at least 40 candidates (about 1% false adoption under exchangeability), and generation uses it from then on.
Controls that isolate the effect:
- In discovery, F keeps design o's original generator, with the same steps, rule, categories, seeds and CPU. S runs R's machinery on values permuted within each step, so it learns from noise.
- On the fresh categories, the frozen final generator G* is paired against G_R0 and G0 in one-step discovery episodes at matched CPU. G_R0 has identical machinery, K and composer, but only the prior: no discovered knowledge, no library, no transplants. G0 is the original generator.
- G* minus G_R0 isolates the effect of what was discovered on how candidates are generated. G* minus G0 is the effect against the original generator.
Not isolated: Route 3 alone (its adoptions and prospective gains are only reported). Design o's own route, where the parent's learning principle adapts the edit distribution, is dropped from R: it was never exercised in 29 steps and cannot be under the measured acceptance limit.
mechanism_changes:
New file rsi6/open/effects.py (about 450 lines):
- featurize(parent, child, info, cell): sparse features of one edit in its context. They are: the cell; the inserted and removed op; the sensor of a load; live before and after; the change of live length; a position bucket; the theta index and whether live code reads it; the sign and size of a perturbation; a scalar's new value; a library or transplant unit id; the parent's count of accepted changes.
- EffectModel (add, fit, draw, predict, digest) fits y_ces = sum_j x_j.(b + b_e) + g*pairs(c) + u_c + w_ce + o_pes + eps. The terms are: b shared and b_e category-specific coefficients, g a pairwise interaction, u_c and w_ce candidate idiosyncrasies, o_pes the offset common to every candidate of parent p on seed s, and eps noise. Gaussian priors are set per feature group. Noise variances start from the measured paired sds (0.021, 0.039, 0.006; bin packing's comes from development). The posterior is closed-form GLS over about 1,300 coefficients. Hyperparameters are set by marginal likelihood on a grid every 4 pooled steps. A CPU sub-model fits log(cpu_c/cpu_p) = sum x.b_cpu.
- compose(): sequential Thompson construction. Each addition draws a pool of 100 single edits of the current macro with edits.apply_edit, drops no-ops by behaviour key, and scores each edit by x.b~ + g~*k. The best edit is added if its score is positive, its target is untouched, and predicted CPU stays at or below 1.15 x generation 0 and 1.06 x parent. Construction stops at k_max(n) or when the probability of exceeding C_TARGET stops rising. Excluded cells are never drawn.
- diff and apply_diff for transplants; structure_variants and prospective_score for Route 3.
New file rsi6/open/discovery_m.py (about 300 lines):
- A fork of discovery.Lineage with the same screen, promote and confirm rules, caps and confirmation-seed windows.
- A PooledGenerator shared by the lineages of an arm, with modes recursive, shuffled, prior and frozen.
- Each candidate's prediction is recorded before its runs. Confirmation runs reach the model only after the decision. The generator's own process CPU is added to the lineage's spent.
- Records: m_step, m_accept, m_structure, m_lineage_done. Arm F uses discovery.Lineage unchanged, in mode frozen.
New file rsi6/open/experiment_m.py (about 450 lines): stages discovery, selection, heldout and meta.
Also new: rsi6/registry/registration_m.json and rsi6/tests/test_effects.py (about 250 lines).
Constants:
- DISCOVERY = jobshop, quadassign, pmedian, binpacking (knapsack dropped: no signal).
- K_MAX = 8, unless development check D3 sets another value by its pre-written rule.
- POOL = 100; EXCLUDE = (-0.01, 0.8); C_TARGET = 0.018.
- STRUCT_PERIOD = 8, STRUCT_T = 2.6, STRUCT_MIN = 40.
- CPU_PER_LINEAGE = 12,000.
Not changed: the kernel (run.py, problem.py, environment.py, ledger.py, roles.py), the meter, the published references, design_o.py, edits.py, discovery.py and evaluate.py, which are imported as they are.
measurement_design:
Discovery, on source categories jobshop, quadassign, pmedian and binpacking at the search budget (train 40, n_train 12, part A). It uses the registered o step:
- 6 candidates are screened on 1 seed;
- the best half of the positive ones are promoted to 2 seeds;
- the best promoted candidate with a value of at least 0.005 is confirmed with its parent on 4 seeds used for nothing else;
- it is accepted if the mean is at least 0.0025, t >= 2.6 over the 16 pairs, and CPU is at most 1.10 x the parent's;
- the screening cap is 1.25 x generation 0.
Arms:
- R: 4 lineages sharing one pooled posterior.
- F: 4 lineages with design o's generator in mode frozen.
- S: 2 lineages with R's machinery, fed values permuted within each step.
Every lineage gets 12,000 CPU-s, including its generator's CPU, and steps are interleaved. Lineage k of every arm uses its own three discovery seeds, shared across arms and distinct across k, so that the pooled model does not carry one parent-seed draw in every measurement. Each lineage also has its own confirmation window.
Selection is as in registration o: part B with 4 selection seeds, and the better lineage of an arm.
Held-out capability, on the four fresh categories, which are unlocked only at this stage, at the run budget with 8 seeds:
- the finals of R, F and S, plus o0 and a0;
- o0, a0, F and S raised pair by pair to R's CPU with evaluate.raise_until; a comparison with a pair that falls short is void;
- every accepted parent of every R and F lineage on 4 seeds (the transfer curve).
Meta stage, the recursion test on the same four categories, run after the capability stage:
- E = min(24, floor(55,000 / CPU of episode 1)) paired episodes; the endpoint is void if E < 12.
- In each episode, G*, G_R0 and G0 each make one registered step from o0 on all four categories, with the episode's shared seeds (screen on 1 seed, promote on 2, part A).
- G* is R's final posterior and structure, frozen, with no library or transplants. G_R0 has the same machinery and K with the prior only. G0 draws cells uniformly with nedit 0.6/0.3/0.1.
- The selected candidate is confirmed with o0 on part B with 4 fresh seeds.
- A control whose episode CPU is below G*'s screens extra candidates until it is not below.
Endpoints:
- E_meta (primary). Y1 is the confirmed 16-pair mean of the episode's selected candidate, 0 if none is ready. E_meta needs three parts: the mean over episodes of Y1(G*) - Y1(G0) above 0, of Y1(G*) - Y1(G_R0) above 0 (one-sided 95% bootstrap intervals over episodes, then categories), and Y1(G*) above 0.
- E_cap: R final - o0@R at least 0.01, with a 95% interval excluding 0, and not void. R - F@R is reported.
- E_learn (source, secondary): acceptances, mean screening value after the 10th pooled step, and prospective Spearman, for R against F and S.
- Also reported: G*'s calibration on the fresh categories, the transfer curve, the structure record, and CPU by arm.
Success condition:
- Recursive improvement of discovery on unseen categories is reported only if all three parts of E_meta hold.
- Recursive improvement of capability acquisition on unseen categories is reported only if, in addition, E_cap holds and R - F@R > 0.
- Anything less is reported as what it is.
Seeds: new registered blocks, disjoint from development and from registration o. The random seed is fixed. The bootstrap uses 5,000 draws seeded by the CRC-32 of the comparison name.
predictions: D0 (development check D3, before registration, source categories): non-excluded macros at k = 8 have a deconvolved 4-category true-effect sd of 0.011 (0.008 to 0.016) and a mean of -0.002; the additivity slope, measured against the summed single-edit predictions, is 0.7
P1 (source): Spearman correlation between R's pre-measurement prediction and the screening value, over R's candidates after its 10th pooled step: +0.30, with an interval excluding 0
P2 (source, same seeds): mean screening value after the 10th pooled step, R minus F: +0.006 (R about -0.004, F about -0.010)
P3 (source, accepted mechanisms over each arm's lineages): R 8 over its four (90% range 2 to 25), F 0.3 over its four (at most 1), S 0.1 over its two (at most 1)
P4 (source): over R's confirmations, mean confirmed value divided by mean promotion value is 0.5 (the same ratio in experiment o: 0.13)
P5 (fresh categories, primary): mean Y1 over episodes is +0.005 for G*, +0.0002 for G0 and 0.000 for G_R0; all three parts of E_meta hold with probability about 0.6
P6 (fresh categories): mean screening value of the generated candidates is -0.004 for G*, -0.010 for G0 and -0.05 for G_R0

P7 (fresh categories): over all G* and G0 candidates of the meta stage, the slope of the measured screening value on G*'s recorded predicted shared effect is +0.4 (above 0), carried by edits predicted to be destructive; among candidates with a positive prediction, the slope is within 0 +/- 0.5
P8 (fresh categories): R final minus o0@R is +0.002 (interval about +/-0.012); E_cap is not met (probability 0.85); R minus F@R is +0.001

P9 (fresh categories): along R's lineages, the held-out acquired score changes by 0.000 per accepted mechanism (-0.004 to +0.004); acceptances on source categories do not accumulate held-out capability
P10: 0 to 2 structure variants are adopted, each with a prospective gain below 0.05 nats per candidate
P11 (source): S's mean screening value is -0.04, below F's: macros built without information are destructive
failure_modes: The single-edit spread is smaller than inferred (sd 0.003 instead of 0.004), or the kept edits are slightly harmful (-0.001 each). The pass probability then falls to 0.03 to 0.085 per step, R accepts 0 to 2 per arm, and only P1 and P2 remain to report.

Edits interact: they are sub-additive, or several edits of one program break it. Macros then have negative means, the interaction term stops composition early, and R degenerates toward single edits, that is, toward F.

Acceptances are category-specific (the measured per-category effect correlation is about 0). R accepts on the source categories, but the fresh categories see only the shared part, about 0 to 0.003 per acceptance. E_cap is null (as predicted) and the transfer curve is flat.

What the model learned does not transfer. On weighted tardiness, UBQP, project scheduling or clique, other edit classes may be destructive, because sensors such as prev, occnext or capleft mean something else or read zeros. Macros of 8 edits compound the error, and G* can be worse than G0: a negative answer for E_meta.
Fresh categories that carry little signal (the knapsack pattern), or far more noise than the source categories, shrink every Y1 toward 0, and the meta endpoint loses power.
CPU drift: macros approach the caps. Refusals waste screening runs, and slower accepted mechanisms give the raised controls more budget.
Pooling couples R's four lineages. One misleading early posterior misdirects all of them, and R has no independent between-lineage replication (F does).

Common parent-seed offsets. If a large share of the paired noise is shared by every candidate of a parent on a seed, the absolute thresholds (screen above 0, promotion value at least the margin) act on shifted values. This is one possible explanation of only 4 confirmations in 29 steps of experiment o, where every lineage screened against o0 on seed 61. The model's offset term and distinct seeds per lineage reduce this but do not remove it.
Structure decisions are scored off-policy, on candidates the incumbent generated. An adopted variant may predict well there and badly where it would generate itself.

The meta stage measures only the first step from o0. An advantage that appears only after parents change is not seen. Part B confirmation (other instance groups) may also be harsher than part A, for every arm.
Bugs in credit assignment or featurisation would give a confident but wrong posterior. Planted-effect tests and the D1 replay are the guard.
The meta stage selects candidates on the fresh categories, so those categories count as used for any later process.
If budget_scaling.json shows better noise per CPU-second at train 200, the numbers here (train 40) are not the best design available.
novelty:
Not new as components: hierarchical Gaussian models with empirical Bayes, Thompson sampling, surrogate-assisted evolution and adaptive operator selection, group screening (changing several factors at once to see small effects), and predicting an edit's effect before applying it (the Owner's reference, arXiv 2610.13991).
Different from design o:
- Design o learns 43 weights per lineage from six values per step with the parent's CEM, and changes its generator only when a new learning principle is adopted, which has not happened.
- Here every measurement of every lineage is pooled, with credit assignment across multi-edit candidates, categories, seeds and CPU.
- The size of a candidate is set from the measured detection limit of the acceptance rule.
- Accepted edit sets move between lineages.
Different from design q: q searches programs inside acquisition with a blind prior on noisy 4-problem batches, and it was starved. This works one level up, on paired fresh-instance measurements, and leaves acquisition unchanged.
New in the evaluation: the generator itself is tested on unseen categories, by its one-step discovery yield against the original generator and against the same machinery without the discovered knowledge, not only through the learner it produced.
Not claimed:
- No new learning principle. The recursion runs through learned knowledge about the edit space, which is closer to learning-to-search than to the discovery of learning principles.
- The most likely positive outcome is partial: better discovery yield on unseen categories, with no detectable gain of the final learner there.
implementation_plan:
1. effects.py and its tests (about 450 + 250 lines, 5 hours). The tests check:
- planted-effect recovery on synthetic data with the measured noise, including posterior coverage and exclusion of destructive cells within 5 measurements;
- that every macro composed from o0 is valid, changes behaviour, uses distinct targets and stays within the CPU predictions;
- determinism of compose and fit;
- the diff/apply_diff round trip.
2. discovery_m.py (about 300 lines, 2 hours): the pooled generator; predictions recorded before measurement; confirmation data entering the model only after the decision; generator CPU charged to the lineage; stop-and-resume replay through append_once.
3. experiment_m.py and registration_m.json (about 450 lines, 3 hours), forked from experiment.py, with the meta stage added.
4. Development checks, on source categories only, with the development ledger and development seeds, in this order:
- D1 (0 CPU): replay experiment o's recorded o_step candidates in step order, fitting before each step and predicting its screening values. Go if the prospective Spearman correlation exceeds 0.1. R's registered prior does not use these data.
- D2 (about 6,000 CPU-s): a --dev run of R, F and S on the four discovery categories with budgets divided by 20, checking records, caps, CPU charging and resume.
- D3 (about 5,500 CPU-s): 8 macros at each k of 1, 4 and 8, and 12 G0 candidates, on 2 seeds; plus o0 and 12 candidates on 8 seeds. This measures the deconvolved mean and sd by k, the additivity slope, CPU ratios, bin packing's paired noise, and the share of paired noise common to a parent's seed. K_MAX is set to the k that maximises the per-step pass probability these estimates give, by a rule written before D3. If that probability is below 0.05 at every k, the registration predicts no acceptance by R and says so.
- D4 (0 CPU): a stub null calibration of false acceptance per step and per lineage, with macros and the new noise profile. The step-power simulation <scratch>/panel/work/generator/step_power.py was written for this proposal but not run (running it was refused here). Running it here replaces the analytic approximations used in this proposal.
5. Two independent code reviews, then registration with file hashes, then the stages in order. The four fresh categories are unlocked only at the held-out stage.
About 1,450 new lines: a day of work, with D1 to D4 running alongside.
compute_budget:
Registered experiment, against the 300,000 CPU-s available:
- Discovery: 120,000. R gets 4 x 12,000, F 4 x 12,000 and S 2 x 12,000; each lineage is charged its runs and its generator's CPU. That is about 20 steps per R lineage at about 36 CPU-s per mechanism-seed on the four categories, or about 480 screened candidates per arm. The 36 CPU-s is estimated from the run budget (bin packing about 35, p-median 9, job shop 5, quadratic assignment 2), scaled by 0.7 for the search budget.
- Selection: about 4,000.
- Held-out capability: at most 30,000. This covers 5 versions and 4 matched controls x 4 categories x 8 seeds at about 2.5 raising levels, plus the transfer curve at 4 seeds.
- Meta stage: at most 55,000. That is 3 generators x 64 runs plus 28 shared o0 runs per episode, 24 episodes at about 10 CPU-s per run; fewer episodes by the registered rule if the fresh categories cost more.
- Total: at most 209,000, leaving about 91,000 for the unmeasured run costs of the fresh categories.
Development before registration, on source categories and outside the 300,000: D2 about 6,000, D3 about 5,500, D1 and D4 none.
